headline: Ordained parking and traffic ordinances and adopted a resolution accepting a $1,923,714.10 state transportation grant; denied reconsideration of immigration-enforcement signage orders.
summary: The council ordained 23 ordinances on parking, traffic signs, and trash placement. It referred dozens of resident petitions to committees and denied reconsideration of two orders on civil immigration enforcement signage. It placed a civilian review board item on file after adopting two police reporting orders.
decisions: Approved the minutes of the July 21, 2026 City Council meeting, 11-0.
Granted National Grid permission for a conduit location on Velander St., 11-0.
Granted National Grid permission for a conduit location at Washington Sq., 11-0.
Granted National Grid and Verizon New England permission for a jointly-owned pole on Christine St., 11-0.
Denied reconsideration of the August 18, 2026 vote on King's order for signage saying property may not be used for civil immigration enforcement, 5-6.
Denied reconsideration of King's order on multilingual signage in the ordinance, 4-7.
Approved reconsideration of King's multilingual signage order, 11-0.
Denied adoption of King's multilingual signage order after reconsideration, 5-6.
Referred petitions 10a through 10c, including a shade tree and tree removals, to the Department of Parks, Recreation and Cemetery, 11-0.
Referred petition 10d on cat roaming regulations to the Public Health and Human Services Committee, 11-0.
Referred petitions 10e through 10x, including streetlight, road repair, and street naming requests, to the Public Works Committee, 11-0.
Referred petitions 10y and 10z on speed limit signage to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Referred petitions 11a through 11z on signs, speed humps, and parking to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Referred petitions 12a through 12n on truck restrictions, parking, and traffic calming to the Traffic and Parking Committee, 11-0.
Referred petition 12o on the European Starling population to the Veterans' Memorials, Parks and Recreation Committee, 11-0.
Placed two constable appointment communications on file, 11-0.
Confirmed Lauren Tiberio, Jennifer Maddox, and John Finn to the Accessibility Advisory Committee, 11-0 for each.
Voted to advertise three proposed ordinances to amend the Salary Ordinance, 11-0.
Referred the DCU Special Tax District Borrowing communication to the Municipal and Legislative Operations Committee, 11-0.
Adopted resolutions on grants and donations, including a $1,923,714.10 state transportation grant, plus related transfers and payments, 11-0.
Adopted 18 committee chairman's orders, including reports on ordinance changes, tobacco revenue, and traffic signs, 11-0.
Referred the Borenstein petition to amend off-street parking requirements for dwellings to the Economic Development Committee, 11-0.
Accepted two Municipal and Legislative Operations reports recommending communications be placed on file, 11-0.
Accepted and adopted Traffic and Parking Committee orders for items 19a through 19g, including signs, speed limits, and crosswalks, 11-0.
Accepted Traffic and Parking reports recommending that petitions 19h through 19z be placed on file, 11-0.
Accepted Traffic and Parking reports recommending that petitions 20a through 20n be placed on file, 11-0.
Ordained 23 ordinances (21a through 21w) on parking, handicap spaces, turn bans, stop signs, loading zones, and trash placement, 11-0.
Withdrew King's motion asking the City Clerk for a copy of a Worcester Regional Research Bureau report on civilian oversight.
Denied Petty's motion to suspend Rule 21 so King could speak beyond 10 minutes on the civilian review board item, 5-6.
Adopted Councilor Mitra's order asking for a biannual report on Worcester Police Department goals and misconduct, 11-0.
Adopted Councilor Ojeda's order asking the Police Chief for a report on rising arrests, 11-0.
Placed the civilian review board report item on file, 8-3, on Rosen's motion.
Placed the Toomey order on a public discussion of the DOJ investigation closure on file, 8-3.
Denied reconsideration of the Toomey order on the DOJ investigation, 7-4.
Adopted King and Economou order asking for research on in-road warning light crosswalk systems, 10-0 with Bilotta absent.
Denied King's order to postpone the August 18, 2026 meeting and move its items to September 8, 2026, 5-5.
Approved suspending the rules to extend the public participation section by one hour, 11-0.
Referred King's motion on joint meetings with the School Committee to the Education Committee, 10-0 with Bilotta absent.
